card.name: Punctuation and links before adverse effects
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods, commas after 'Afterward', and linking words like 'lead to' or 'result in' that come right before a side effect or what happens next. Seen in blood-draw descriptions and NSAID or TNF blocker warnings.

modes.label: Blood draw aftermath
modes.description: A period or the comma after 'Afterward' in text describing how a needle stick feels and what follows.
modes.example: When the needle pricks your arm, you may feel a slight stinging sensation or pain<<.>> Afterward, the site may be slightly

modes.label: Cause-and-effect links
modes.description: The word 'to' or 'in' after 'can lead' or 'may result' just before a named effect.
modes.example: NSAIDs, including meloxicam, can lead<< to>> new onset or worsening of preexisting hypertension

modes.label: Heading comma
modes.description: A comma inside a warning section heading listing several adverse conditions.
